headline: Approved REIB Impact Assessment Memo on Burlington Forward resolution, forwarding it to City Council
summary: The committee discussed proposed changes to the Equity Impact Assessment Memo on the Burlington Forward resolution, including language on public safety, community engagement, and attaching written community feedback. The committee then voted to approve the memo and send it to City Council.
decisions: Approved the Equity Impact Assessment Memo and its recommendations and forwarded it to City Council.

decision_evidence.quote: Councilor Grant made a motion to approve the memo and its recommendations and forward it to City Council. ... Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson seconded the motion. The motion passed, the memo was approved and will be forwarded to City Council.

• Call to Order 
o Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson called the meeting to order at 12:32 pm. 
• Approve Agenda & Minutes  
o Councilor Grant moved to approve the agenda and minutes. Councilor Carpenter seconded. The motion 
passed unanimously. 
• Public Forum 
o Public Forum closed with no comments. 
• Equity Impact Assessment Memo: Burlington Forward: A Comprehensive Framework For Safe Public Spaces 
And A Stronger Community 
o Councilor Carpenter discussed adding language to clarify that the resolution is intended to address a 
subgroup of individuals whose conduct has impacted public safety and use of public spaces, rather than 
unhoused people generally. 
▪ Councilor Grant expressed concern about identifying or categorizing people and emphasized the 
need to distinguish homelessness, substance use, mental illness, poverty, and criminal conduct. 
She emphasized that the focus should be on conduct and root causes rather than identifying 
groups of people. Refer to the video. 
o Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson revised the language to emphasize criminal conduct in public spaces and 
beyond/citywide.  
o Councilor Carpenter explained that the intent was to use the Council committee structure to gather 
feedback on the resolution. Refer to the video. 
▪ Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson said there should have been a more intentional community 
engagement process before the resolution was introduced.  
▪ Councilor Grant emphasized that this concern has been raised previously and that resolutions 
should include input from Councilors, City staff, department heads, community stakeholders, 
social service organizations, and mutual aid groups.
o Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson noted that there was not enough information to verify what preliminary 
community input was received before the resolution was introduced. The reference to preliminary input 
was removed from the memo. 
▪ Councilor Carpenter discussed the challenges of conducting community engagement while 
complying with Open Meeting Laws. Refer to the video. 
o Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson agreed to include additional written feedback from community members 
and organizations as attachments to the memo. Refer to the video. 
• Recommended Action: Motion for the Committee to approve the memo and its recommendations and 
forward it to the City Council for consideration 
o Councilor Grant made a motion to approve the memo and its recommendations and forward it to City 
Council. 
o Councilor Carpenter expressed concern that the memo did not dully acknowledge the intent of the 
resolution’s sponsors and was hesitant to endorse it without additional clarification.  
▪ Councilor Grant emphasized the importance of considering the impact of the resolution on 
community members, not only the intent of its authors. Refer to the video. 
o Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson seconded the motion. The motion passed, the memo was approved and 
will be forwarded to City Council. 
• Adjournment 
o Councilor Sanchez-Parkinson adjourned the meeting at 1:30 pm.
